pages.title: Meeting new people

situation.text: You are new in the neighborhood. In the park, a stranger smiles at you. You greet them, say your name, ask where they are from and make small talk.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can introduce yourself, ask someone’s origin and have a friendly 30-second chat with a new person.
canDo: Say where you are from: I’m from…
Ask: Are you…? / Where are you from?
Start small talk about the weather and the place
success: I say hello and my name.
I end the chat with a smile.
pages.think: In Portuguese, how do you introduce yourself to a stranger in a park? Do you say your full name or just your first name?

teach.goal: Abrir pela situação real: ser “o novo” e encontrar um vizinho.
solo: Leia o objetivo e peça que o estudante diga, em português, o que faria ao conhecer alguém no parque.
Mostre os 4 critérios de sucesso: é a missão final.
group: Cada estudante diz o próprio primeiro nome em inglês, devagar.
Mostre a cena e pergunte: Who are they? Where are they?
extra: Do you like meeting new people?
Where do you usually meet new people?
support: Aceite respostas em português e reformule em inglês, uma frase curta por vez.

pages.title: Connection & warm-up

intro.solo: Start with easy personal questions; the student answers with one or two words.
intro.group: Each student answers one question and asks it back to the next person.

pages.recall: Primeira aula da unidade: não há conteúdo anterior. Verifique o que o estudante já sabe: Hello, Goodbye, Thank you.
pages.tip: Listen for words the student already knows. Celebrate every English sentence, even a short one.

teach.goal: Entrar no inglês no primeiro minuto e medir o ponto de partida.
extra: How do you say your name? Can you spell it?
What English words do you already know?

errors.w: My name is Ana, I have 20 years.

support: Ofereça as respostas-modelo e peça que apenas escolham uma.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Meeting people in the USA
pages.intro: In the USA, people often use first names quickly, even with someone they just met. Look at the cards and guess before you read.

cards.note: People say “I’m Ken” — not “Mr. Tanaka” — in most casual situations.
“Nice day, isn’t it?” is an easy way to start talking to a stranger.
It is usually a greeting, not a real question. The normal answer is “Good, thanks. You?”

qs.q: What do people say when they meet someone new?
qs.pt: O que se diz ao conhecer alguém?

levels.A1: Hi! I’m Ana. Nice to meet you.
levels.A2: They say their first name and “Nice to meet you.”
levels.B1: They greet, give their first name, say “Nice to meet you” and often smile or shake hands.
levels.B2: A brief exchange of first names, a smile or a handshake, and a light question keeps the moment friendly.

qs.q: What topics are easy for small talk?
qs.pt: Que assuntos são fáceis para um papo leve?

levels.A2: The weather, the place, the weekend.
levels.B1: The weather, the neighborhood, work or plans for the weekend.
levels.B2: Neutral topics such as the weather, the place you are in, or work, rather than money or politics.

qs.q: Is “How are you?” a real question?
qs.pt: “How are you?” é uma pergunta de verdade?

levels.B1: Usually it is a greeting; a short, positive answer is expected.
levels.B2: In casual contexts it works as a greeting, so a long answer would surprise people, unless you are talking with a close friend.

pages.compare: In Brazil many people greet with a kiss on the cheek or a hug, and “Tudo bem?” is similar to “How are you?”. In the USA, a smile, a wave or a handshake is more common with strangers. What do you do where you live?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto cultural: nomes, cumprimentos e small talk.
solo: Mostre os 3 cartões e peça hipóteses antes de explicar.
Compare com o “Tudo bem?” brasileiro: ambos são cumprimentos, não perguntas reais.
group: Cada estudante escolhe um cartão e explica em uma frase.
Pergunte “Is it the same in Brazil?”.
answers: Q1: Hi! I’m… Nice to meet you.
Q3: normalmente é um cumprimento; resposta curta: Good, thanks. You?
extra: Do you like small talk?
Who do you greet with a kiss or a hug?
support: Use as respostas A1 como modelo e peça que repitam.
stretch: B2: explique por que respostas muito longas a “How are you?” podem causar estranhamento.

teach.goal: Entender a situação antes de ver o texto: ideia principal e depois 4–5 informações.
solo: Esconda o texto. 1ª escuta: só a ideia principal.
2ª escuta: países, clima, profissão e rua.
Mostre o texto só depois.
group: Escuta coletiva; duplas anotam antes de revelar.
Compare as respostas entre as duplas.
answers: Pass 1: meeting for the first time.
Pass 2: Japan · Brazil · sunny · chef · Maple Street.
extra: Who is new in the neighborhood?
How do they say goodbye?

qs.q: Is Mia new in the neighborhood?

retell.prompt: Retell the conversation in your own words, at your level.

teach.goal: Ler o diálogo, perceber os chunks e recontar.
solo: O estudante lê o papel de Mia; você lê o de Ken. Depois troquem.
Peça um reconto curto em 3 frases.
group: Leitura em duplas com troca de papéis.
Reconto em cadeia: uma frase por estudante.
answers: Japan · yes, she is · chef · sunny
extra: What would you say after “See you around”?
What else can they talk about?

errors.w: I am from Brazil, and you?
errors.r: I’m from Brazil. Where are you from?

support: Mostre a tradução (botão PT) depois da 2ª leitura.

pages.title: Useful expressions

items.use: Say your name or a simple fact about you.
Say it right after you hear someone’s name.
Ask a yes/no question about a person.
Ask about someone’s country or city.
Explain why you are asking things.

items.pt: A gente se vê por aí!
items.use: A friendly goodbye to someone nearby.

pages.note: Choose 3–5 expressions (★) to use again and again today: I’m… · Nice to meet you · Where are you from?

teach.goal: Escolher 4 chunks para uso repetido e descobrir a função de cada um.
solo: Pergunte “When do you say it?” antes de traduzir.
Peça um exemplo próprio para cada ★.
group: Cada estudante escolhe uma expressão e explica quando usa.
Duplas: apresentem-se com as 4 expressões.
answers: Introducing · Reacting · Asking about origin · Saying goodbye
extra: Which one do you say first when you meet someone?
Which one is more casual?

errors.w: Nice to meet-you too, my pleasure.

support: Trabalhe só I’m… e Nice to meet you na primeira rodada.

swap.tpt: Oi! Eu sou {name}. Eu sou de {place}.

head: Spoken English
Written English
rows: Yes, I recently moved to this area.
It is a pleasure to meet you.
register.note: Contractions (I’m, you’re) are natural in speech and in informal writing. In formal emails, you may write I am.

teach.goal: Fixar “I’m…” e “Are you…?”; os demais são expansão. Usar a troca de palavras para variar a fala.
solo: Mostre os padrões DENTRO do diálogo.
Use “Swap the words”: o estudante diz a frase completa a cada troca.
Compare spoken × written em 2 exemplos.
group: Troca em cadeia: cada estudante muda UMA peça.
Em pares: A escolhe as peças e B fala.
teach.answers: Padrões 01/02 são o foco; 03/04 são expansão.
extra: Change the name and the place and say the new sentence.
Make it a question: You’re from Japan → Are you from Japan?
support: Fique só com “I’m + nome” e “I’m from + lugar” na primeira rodada.
stretch: Combine: I’m Ken. I’m from Japan. Are you from here?

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: English has strong and weak syllables. Stress the important word: “I’m MI-a.” “NICE to MEET you.” The goal is clarity, not a perfect accent.

own.prompt: Write one sentence about you: “I’m from…”. Mark the strong syllable.
own.criteria: Say it twice: first flat, then with stress. Can your partner hear the strong word?

teach.goal: UM só fenômeno: sílaba forte (ritmo) em frases curtas.
solo: Modele com palmas na sílaba forte.
Peça que o estudante marque a sílaba forte da própria frase.
group: Coro; depois duplas ouvindo e apontando a sílaba forte.
Cada estudante diz a frase própria.
answers: Identify 1: Where are you from? · Identify 2: I’m from Japan.

errors.w: bra-ZIL pronunciado Brasil /brazil/ sem stress final

errors.r: NICE to MEET you (as palavras pequenas são fracas)

support: Reduza a velocidade e conte as batidas em voz alta.

levels.h: Controlled practice — choose the best answer

items.q: 1. Someone says: “Hi, I’m Sam.” What do you say?
opts: Nice to meet you, Sam. I’m Ana.
items.why: Answer the name with Nice to meet you and say yours.

items.q: 2. You want to know the other person’s country.
4. Someone asks: “How are you?” What is a natural answer?
items.why: “How are you?” is a greeting; keep it short.

levels.h: Guided practice — complete, substitute and transform

items.text: Hi! I’m Mia. Nice to ___ you.
___ you from here? — No, I’m not.

items.npc: It’s a beautiful day, isn’t it?
items.why: Agree and keep the small talk going.

teach.goal: Do controlado ao guiado: completar, transformar e responder antes da fala livre.
solo: Peça que o estudante justifique cada resposta.
Se acertar rápido, peça a versão com “And you?”.
group: Resolvam em duplas e comparem antes de revelar.
Equipes: ponto por resposta justificada.
answers: 1: Nice to meet you, Sam. I’m Ana. · 2: Where are you from? · 3: I’m from Mexico. · 4: Good, thanks. You?
Gap: meet · Are · Are you from Japan? · I’m from Brazil. · I’m from Brazil. And you? · Yes, it’s sunny!
extra: Say each correct answer aloud with a smile.
support: Ofereça o banco de palavras nas lacunas.

pages.title: Personalized roleplay — meet a new neighbor

brief.teacher: You are a friendly stranger in the park (ask one extra question each round).
brief.student: You are new in town: introduce yourself and make small talk.

orders: Meet a neighbor in a park
Meet a classmate on the first day
Meet a coworker at a coffee machine
complications: The stranger speaks fast: ask them to repeat.
You didn’t catch their name: ask again.
They ask a question you don’t know: say “I’m not sure.”
The conversation goes quiet: ask about the weather.
success: I say hello and my name.
I end the chat with a smile.

teach.goal: Simulação com complicações e três rodadas com menos apoio.
solo: Use um cenário real do estudante (novo trabalho, novo curso).
Rodada 1: com chunks. 2: só palavras-chave. 3: sem roteiro.
Meta de fala: 60–70% para o estudante. Anote 2–3 correções.
extra: What if the stranger doesn’t say anything?
How do you ask someone to repeat their name?

errors.r: Sorry, can you say that again?
My name is Rafa. / I’m Rafa.

support: Volte à rodada 1 se travar; peça só a primeira frase.
stretch: Apresente uma terceira pessoa: This is my friend…

rounds.title: Meet & greet
rounds.task: Say your name and say “Nice to meet you.”

rounds.title: Where from?
rounds.task: Ask where your partner is from.
rounds.hint: Where are you from? / I’m from…

rounds.title: Small talk
rounds.task: Talk about the weather and the place.

rounds.title: Introduce a partner
rounds.task: Whole group: introduce your last partner.

infogap.title: Who is who?
infogap.instr: Ask your partner and complete your card. Do not look at the other card!

a.title: Card A
a.task: You know Sara and Leo. Ask about Omar and Yuki.

b.title: Card B
b.task: You know Omar and Yuki. Ask about Sara and Leo.

teach.goal: Fluência por repetição das apresentações com informações novas a cada rodada.
group: Troque os pares a cada rodada (A+B / C+D → A+C / B+D → A+D / B+C → grupo).
Responsabilidade individual: cada aluno faz ≥1 pergunta e ≥1 resposta.
Na rodada final, cada um apresenta o último parceiro ao grupo.
answers: Info gap: Sara = Egypt · Leo = Italy · Omar = Morocco · Yuki = Japan.
extra: Is Omar from Spain? (No, he isn’t.)
Where is Yuki from?
support: Entregue frases-modelo no chat da turma.

pages.title: Group mission — your first day in the neighborhood
pages.goal: Each group must meet someone new in English: greet, introduce, ask, make small talk and say goodbye.

missions.mission: Meet someone at the park. Find out their name and country. Mention the weather.
It is the first day of a course. Meet two new people and remember both names.
You meet a new coworker at lunch. Learn where they are from and say you are new, too.
missions.constraint: Say “I’m new here” and close with “See you around!”

success: Say one thing about the weather or the place.
Say goodbye in a friendly way.

teach.goal: Realizar algo com o inglês: conhecer alguém e manter a conversa.
group: Cada grupo recebe papel, restrição e missão. Alternem de papel.
Progressão: 1ª rodada com frases de apoio, 2ª só palavras-chave, 3ª sem roteiro.
Anote 2–3 correções prioritárias.
answers: Modelo: “Hi! I’m Ana. Nice to meet you.” → “I’m Tom. Are you from here?” → “No, I’m from Brazil. Where are you from?”
extra: What if you forget the other person’s name?
support: Dê o início de frase em cada cartão.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short message to a new neighbor. Say hello, give your name, say where you are from and invite them for coffee.
pages.model: Hi! **I’m Ana.** I’m your new neighbor. **I’m from** Brazil. Where are you from? **Nice to meet you!** See you around!
checklist: I wrote my name with I’m… / My name is…
I said where I am from.
I asked one question and closed politely.
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta ligada à situação comunicativa.
solo: Peça a mensagem; corrija 2–3 pontos e mostre uma forma mais natural.
group: Cada estudante escreve; troquem os textos e corrijam em duplas.
extra: Add one more question for your neighbor.

errors.w: I am Ana and I am from the Brazil.

support: Dê o modelo e peça só para trocar os dados.

criteria.name: Fluency
criteria.desc: Mantém a comunicação sem interrupções excessivas.

criteria.name: Language use
criteria.desc: Utiliza adequadamente padrões, vocabulário e expressões.

criteria.name: Pronunciation
criteria.desc: É compreensível e usa ritmo e entonação adequados.

criteria.name: Interaction
criteria.desc: Responde, pergunta, esclarece e desenvolve a conversa.

interpret.text: Needs more support. Revisit the main patterns with guided practice before the next lesson.
Functional performance. Work on the lowest criteria in the next lesson.
Good control. Raise complexity and speed; add follow-up questions.
Strong performance. Move to a more demanding situation.

prompts.well: Example: You said your name clearly and asked “Where are you from?” without notes.
prompts.improve: Example: Stress the important word in “Nice to MEET you.”
prompts.next: Example: Introduce a friend to someone new.

teach.goal: Avaliar o que o aluno conseguiu comunicar, não só os erros.
solo: O estudante se autoavalia primeiro; depois você.
Feche com: What you did well · What to improve · Your next challenge.
group: Dê um comentário por critério a cada estudante.
Cada um escolhe o próprio desafio.
teach.answers: A rubrica é uma ferramenta interna de acompanhamento, não uma certificação CEFR.

tasks.name: Build a question
tasks.prompt: Without notes: ask where someone is from.

tasks.name: Respond to a situation
tasks.prompt: Someone says: “Hi, I’m Tom. Nice to meet you.”
tasks.model: Nice to meet you, Tom. I’m Ana.

tasks.name: Use a new expression
tasks.prompt: Say goodbye in a friendly way.

items: Record a 30–45 second audio introducing yourself.
Write 3 sentences about a person you know: name, country, job.
Say hello in English to one person this week (or to the mirror!).
Listen to the dialogue again and note two expressions.

teach.goal: Toda aula termina com uma produção observável.
solo: Sem anotações: uma pergunta, uma resposta e uma expressão nova.
group: Exit challenge individual; compare com o colega.
answers: Where are you from? · Nice to meet you, Tom. I’m Ana. · See you around!
extra: Revisão espaçada: retomar na aula 2, depois de uma semana e no Mission Day.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: The structure stays the same; language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.say: Hi, I’m Ana. I’m from Brazil.
Hi! I’m Ana. I just moved here from Brazil. Are you from here?
ladder.goal: Add context and ask a follow-up question.

ladder.say: Hi, I’m Ana. I’ve just moved to this neighborhood, so I’m still getting to know the area.
ladder.goal: Explain your situation and keep the conversation going.

ladder.say: I’m Ana, nice to meet you. I’ve only been here a couple of weeks, so any tips about the neighborhood would be great.
ladder.goal: Build rapport and ask for advice.

ladder.say: Lovely to meet you. I’m still finding my feet here, so I’d really appreciate any local recommendations.
ladder.goal: Use idiomatic, warm language with ease.

ladder.say: Pleased to meet you. I’m a newcomer to the area, so I’m gladly accepting advice on where to find a decent coffee.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
solo: Mostre onde o estudante está e a próxima etapa.
group: Cada um escolhe a frase do próprio nível e a do próximo.
